chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a sacrificial animal for his Tamattu' Hajj, brought it to his house, tied it up, but it broke free and died. Is it sufficient for him, or must he replace it? He said, 'It is not sufficient for him unless he had no power to control it.'
And if the sacrificial animal incurs a minor defect, there is no harm in selling it, except that its price should be given in charity, and the replacement is upon its owner. He narrated that.

key_terms.لَا قُوَّةَ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ: He had no power to control it
key_terms.لِمُتْعَتِهِ: For his Tamattu' (a type of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim's sacrificial animal dies or is defective before slaughter?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions under which a pilgrim is exempt from re-offering a sacrificial animal (hady) for Tamattu' Hajj, distinguishing between accidental death due to inability to control the animal versus negligence. It further establishes the jurisprudence for animals with minor defects, allowing their sale with the proceeds given as charity while requiring the owner to provide a replacement, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise ritual validity. This ruling underscores the balance between divine mercy in cases of genuine incapacity and the requirement of complete fulfillment of the Hajj obligation.
